newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand wants to see baht strong offshore.
newsitem.headline: Thailand wants to see baht strong offshore.

text.p: Bank of Thailand deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Wednesday the central bank preferred see the baht stronger offshore than in local market to curb any pressure on the currency.

"The stronger baht in overseas market is the direction that the central bank would like it to be. This will hinder any speculation against the baht and ease concerns about possible baht devaluation," Chaiyawat told reporters.
The central bank's move to cut off baht supply to offshore parties won't affect the policy to liberalise financial market and the capital inflows, he said.
"Some normal foreign exchange activities would remain intact. The central bank has not controlled the (genuine) capital inflow," he said.
Since the beginning of this month, there has been no unusual outflow of foreign funds, he said. "On the contrary, there has been some amount of foreign inflows."
Chaiyawat did not reveal the amount of the inflows.
